links.outcome: Local performance of RAPID ICH versus prior studies on consecutive ED NCCTs
links.effect: Sensitivity 87.3%, specificity 74%, PPV 21.3%, NPV 98.6%; 8 false negatives and 203 false positives among 844 NCCTs. Lower than prior RAPID ICH studies.
links.quote: RAPID ICH's sensitivity and specificity were lower than in prior studies performed using RAPID ICH, and there was a high number of false-positive RAPID ICH identifications, limiting the generalizability of the assessed version of this DL tool.

links.outcome: Comparison of AI tool with first-year radiology resident on the same CT scans
links.effect: Resident: 95.2% sensitivity, 90.8% specificity, 45.5% PPV, 99.6% NPV vs RAPID ICH 87.3%, 74%, 21.3%, 98.6%.
links.quote: RAPID ICH showed 87.3% sensitivity, 74% specificity, 21.3% PPV, and 98.6% NPV, while the first-year radiology resident achieved 95.2% sensitivity, 90.8% specificity, 45.5% PPV, and 99.6% NPV.

screen.reason: This is an external validation study assessing the diagnostic performance of a commercial deep learning tool (RAPID ICH) compared to a radiology resident on retrospective emergency department CT scans. It evaluates model accuracy rather than a specific deployment guardrail or practice.
